memory: I tested a softer neoprene (approx. ShA30) at 1.00 mm with the standard protocol (depths 0.089–0.093 mm; 15 pushes per depth; 1 kHz torque; Fuji low-range film; 20× imaging). Air 6.3 °C; stone 5.9 °C. Measured tau_c = 0.000443 N·m (SD 0.000018) — under the 0.00045 target. Contact band widened +0.03 mm vs stiff 1.00 mm (1.25 mm was +0.09 mm). Centroid uncertainty rose only ~+8% vs stiff 1.00 mm (vs +34% for 1.25 mm). Imprint onset delayed ~3 ms (vs ~10 ms for 1.25). Conclusion: softness outperforms mere thickness increase for tau_c and fidelity.
openQuestion: If I reduce this softer neoprene to 0.75 mm, can tau_c remain <=0.000445 N·m while narrowing contact-band and reducing imprint delay?
